title: Add the missing real-tree Fact for the file-row settle branch (root-level stale hardlink file, per O-018)
how_to_read: Each attempt is one line and a `details` filename in this same directory. Open a detail file ONLY when this index points you at one -- the summaries are here so you do not have to. `caused_by` is what sent the stage back; `changed` is what the attempt then touched, counted by kind. Several attempts in a row that were caused by the same stage and changed no `src` is a loop, not progress.

open.issue: observed: Assert.True() Failure at FileRowRevisedGuardTests.cs:99: "of 344 test units in tests/FsAnalyser.Core.Tests read, 0 build a hardlinked name directly under the scan root that is grown through another name and then scanned, and none of them asserts that File row Revised."

C1 (derived from the title and the 'Expected' line): tests/FsAnalyser.Core.Tests has a real-tree Fact that hardlinks a name directly under the scan root to a file in a subfolder, grows the file through the subfolder's name, scans, and asserts the root-level File row is Done at the grown size with Revised true: missing

C2 (derived from 'nothing guards it'): the default suite fails when the file-row half of the latch is broken, i.e. a mutant `r.Kind != EntryKind.File &&` at TopLevelTracker.Build's latch is killed: missing

Where the mutant-A kill lives. Chosen: a one-off check in a disposable copy at build and validate, following Mutants.ps1's safety discipline but adding nothing to it. Alternative: add a TopLevelTracker entry to SL-102's Mutants.ps1 ValidateSet roster so the kill is repeatable. Lesson #428 says 'apply mutants only through Mutants.ps1'. Against that, the roster is SL-102's last-access set, and widening it changes what SL-102's 'All' run means.

Whether the Fact belongs in HardlinkTests, next to ALoneNameUnderTheRootIsChargedAtItsOwnSize, which already builds the root-level stale shape. It is placed in TopLevelTests because Watch and its watcher are private there, and the guarded behaviour is the top-level row, not the hardlink charge.
No standing mutant roster for TopLevelTracker and no change to SL-102's Mutants.ps1 ValidateSet. The design filed it for later.

No Windows 10 run (O-009 is owed to validate-slice). The NTFS per-name staleness was measured only on Windows 11 build 26200, and the Fact would fail loudly at its snapshot-0 assert, not pass vacuously, if Windows 10 behaved differently.

No fixture for a junction or symlink inside a scratch copy, or for a delete denied by an ACL. The corpus's bounded_by line says these are out of the class: a copy is made of plain files in the user's own temp.

Nothing runs tests/bugs/SL-105-FileRowRevisedGuard/ScratchRootCorpus.Tests.ps1 or Mutants.ps1 on a routine basis. They sit outside FsAnalyser.slnx like the other tests/bugs scripts (Q-249). Register them as catalog rows if the person wants the mutant kill re-proved at every later validate.
A standing, repeatable mutant roster for TopLevelTracker (the kind-gated latch, and Seed building before Settle), as the design filed. Run it when src/FsAnalyser.Core/TopLevel*.cs changes.

HardlinkTests.ALoneNameUnderTheRootIsChargedAtItsOwnSize builds the same root-level stale shape and still never asserts TopLevel. It is not the right home for the guard, but its comment could point to the new Fact.

deviation: Mutants.ps1 builds tests/FsAnalyser.Core.Tests/FsAnalyser.Core.Tests.csproj (with its project references) --no-incremental, not FsAnalyser.slnx as SL-102's does, and runs the TopLevel filter, not the whole suite. The slnx build adds the WPF App and the other projects for no benefit here, and the engine's case runner ends a case at 120 s (Q-222). The run takes 42 s.

deviation: The sweep shuts the build servers down once before the first removal, not once per stale root. m1 said 'for each'. The copies carry no SDK of their own because DOTNET_ROOT points at the worktree's .dotnet, and build servers are shared per SDK, so a per-root shutdown would repeat the same call.

deviation: A directory under the fsa-sl105-mutant- prefix with no process id in its name (the form the design's prose gave: fsa-sl105-mutant-<guid>) is treated as stale and swept, since nothing else makes that prefix. Corpus row S07.

deviation: The design counted three files for this slice (the Fact plus the two repro source files). The accepted M1 and m1 findings added four more under the slice's own tests/bugs folder: Mutants.ps1, ScratchRoots.ps1, ScratchRootCorpus.json and ScratchRootCorpus.Tests.ps1. Nothing outside the slice's folder changed apart from TopLevelTests.cs.

drift: None undeclared. Every departure from the design is either an accepted critique disposition or a declared deviation: the committed Mutants.ps1, ScratchRoots.ps1 and the corpus (M1 and m1, which replaced the design's 'no script is committed'), the assert order (m2), one build-server shutdown instead of one per root, the csproj build instead of the slnx build, and the sweep of legacy-named copies (S07).

drift: Mutants.ps1 copies SL-102's helpers Get-SrcDigest, Set-Sdk, Read-Trx and Invoke-Dn instead of sharing them. The M1 disposition asked for a separate script modelled on SL-102's, so this is by decision, but the two copies can now drift apart. Finding m1 is the first case: SC-301 lives in both.
drift: No new drift in round 2. Both new findings are in the m1 corpus runner, which exists by an accepted disposition and is not a departure from the design.

not reviewed: .taad/slices/SL-105/*.json (critique-1, critique-review-1, design-slice-1, design-slice-2, index, build-slice-1): engine records, not code. Per the index rule I left other stages' accounts unread.
not reached: Windows 10 (O-009, Q-192/Q-224): NTFS per-name hardlink staleness and the Fact were measured only on Windows 11 builds 26200 (host) and 26100.9457 (Sandbox).

not reached: A real stale hardlink on a real drive, scanned by the shipped exe. For example, C:\Windows' 14 multi-name root files, which the investigation found 0 stale. Every run here used test fixtures under temp.

not reached: Defender opening the stale name between the Append and the scan, at Defender defaults. Defender was not running in the Sandbox, and on this PC I did not read its state, so the stale fixture was tested against a running Defender only incidentally.
not reached: A File row corrected in OnDisk only or Bytes only (criterion 10). No fixture creates that shape.
not reached: The WPF App showing '(revised)' on a root-level File row. The slice is test-only and the App was not driven.
not reached: The 2 TopLevel symlink tests on the Sandbox could not run without Developer Mode. On this PC they pass (Developer Mode on, Q-001).

critique missed: The critique's M1 fix told the builder to end the committed Mutants.ps1 with 'a src hash plus `git diff --exit-code -- src`'. That is SL-102's SC-301 defect: the check returns 1 whenever src was dirty before the run, even though the script's own digest exists for that case. The critique did not ask what the closing check does when src has uncommitted edits, and it did not check the open defects on the script it told the builder to model on.

critique missed: The design imported 'NTFS per-name staleness holds on Windows 10' as status must-verify. The critique did not ask which stage could discharge it when no Windows 10 machine exists and Q-192/Q-224 already record that. It became O-009, which halted validate once and was waived to SC-330.

code-review missed: The first-pass code review accepted ScratchRootCorpus.Tests.ps1 starting its live non-PowerShell process as `cmd /c ping -n 120 127.0.0.1` and stopping only cmd.exe. ping.exe outlives the run by up to about 120 s, which contradicts the header's 'stops what it started'. A first-pass check of the script's cleanup path (kill what you start) would have found it.

code-review missed: The first-pass review passed the corpus check labelled 'the build servers were shut down once, before anything was removed'. That check asserts only `$State.Released -eq 1`. Moving `& $Release` after the removal loop in ScratchRoots.ps1 still exits 0 with all 11 rows held, so the ordering that m1 asked for is guarded by nothing. A mutation of the new corpus's own checks would have shown it.

still unknown: Is tests/bugs/SL-105-FileRowRevisedGuard registered as a bug-catalog row and re-run at every later validate? The design's claim is recalled from Q-249 and Q-250 and never checked against the running engine. If it is not registered, the repro guards nothing after merge, and only the Fact in the default suite remains. Neither Mutants.ps1 nor the corpus runner is run by anything routine.

still unknown: Does NTFS per-name hardlink staleness hold on Windows 10 (SC-330, Q-192/Q-224)? If it does not, the Fact goes red at TopLevelTests.cs:136 on a Windows 10 machine and cannot be skipped, because CountingRuleTestsAreNeverSkipped covers it. The Fact is measured only on Windows 11 builds 26200 and 26100.9457.

still unknown: Does Defender at defaults open the stale name between the Append and the scan on a machine where it is running? On the host the Fact never saw it (63 spike, 15 validate and 10 Sandbox runs). Validate did not read Defender's state on the host, and Defender was not running in the Sandbox.

still unknown: Mutant C (Seed builds the row before Settle) is killed by 2 existing TopLevel tests, but the investigation never captured their failure messages. It is unknown whether they die for the right reason (the watcher's 'Revised in the snapshot it settled in' assertion) or by accident. This matters before any standing TopLevelTracker mutant roster is built.

went wrong: Five stages ran twice (build-check, design-slice, critique, code-review, validate-slice) and none of the second runs changed the Fact. The reasons were: design #1 hit a provider session limit; build-check #1 read its own 'Nothing of this slice exists yet' wording as 'partial'; critique #1 and code-review #1 waited on dispositions; validate #1 halted on the unsatisfiable O-009. The reruns overstate how hard the slice was, but they cost real gate time.

went wrong: The design's file count was wrong in the way lesson #388 warns about. It cited #388 and checked only that no test pins TopLevelTests' method names. The undercount came from the critique's M1 and m1 remedies instead (3 files promised, 7 delivered).

went wrong: Mutants.ps1 shipped with a known defect. The critique's M1 fix text prescribed the `git diff --exit-code -- src` closing check (SC-301). Code review found it, and the disposition said 'not deferred'. O-013 was then waived to SC-326. The committed guard still exits 1 whenever src was already dirty, which is exactly the case it is run for (uncommitted TopLevel*.cs work).

went wrong: The ping.exe orphan (R2-m2) was waived to SC-327 as minor, although the fix is one line. Validate then re-observed it and recorded a failed check, and every later run of ScratchRootCorpus.Tests.ps1 leaves a ping.exe behind. The R2-m3 ordering check is still unguarded (SC-328): the corpus can say 'before anything was removed' while checking only a count.
went wrong: Validate #1 halted solely on O-009 (Windows 10). The design had already said this was open under Q-192/Q-224. It still became an obligation that no stage could discharge.

went wrong: Spike 1 repeated build-check's mutant measurement. The design stage then restated spike 1's diff as its single proposal. The test-only slice paid for the same experiment in three stages (build-check, spike 1, build).

went wrong: The 'engine TEMP' case (C-006) survived into the design and into Mutants.ps1's -Temp Engine/Ordinary arms even though spike 2 had shown it is location-neutral (ChooseTestsRoot redirects the fixture). It roughly doubled the script's runtime for no extra coverage.

went wrong: All six critique and code-review dispositions (3 + 3) were answered by a model and none was triaged by a person (Q-251 already open). The first Sandbox validation run, as SYSTEM, was invalid and had to be redone.
